keyRules: Maximum altitude: 122 m (400 ft) above ground level in the Open Category (uncontrolled airspace)

Open Category: flying within aerodrome control zones (CTR) is prohibited. In controlled airspace, within 5 km of runway thresholds: maximum 43 m and never in the approach or take-off surfaces; greater height requires authorization from the air navigation service provider.
Heliports: flying within 1 nautical mile (1.85 km) of the reference point (HRP) is prohibited; between 1 and 2 nautical miles, maximum 150 ft (46 m) above the heliport, unless coordinated in advance.

Flying is prohibited over military, security or prison facilities and within 1 nautical mile (1.85 km) of them; over refineries, power plants or fuel depots without the owner's permission; and within 25 m (vertically or laterally) of high-voltage power lines.
You must keep a safe distance from people and buildings not involved in the operation.
Always keep the drone within direct line of sight (VLOS) in the Open Category
Piloting or acting as an observer within 8 hours of consuming alcohol or under the influence of psychoactive substances is prohibited.
Night flights: ANAC Res. 312/2026 (May 2026) removed the general restriction in RAAC 100; ANAC's guidance still lists night operations as Specific Category — check with ANAC before flying at night.

Drones weighing less than 250 g are exempt from registration, licensing and mandatory insurance (Resolution 550/2025, August 2025). Drones from 250 g to 25 kg do not require a pilot license, but must be registered digitally with ANAC in the Casillero Aeronáutico Digital (CAD).
Drones weighing ≥250 g: mandatory registration with CAD (ANAC) — no pilot license required in the Open Category
Operations in a Specific Category (25–150 kg or urban flights/BVLOS): require a pilot license, medical certification, and a commercial operator certificate
The Open Category allows drones from 250 g to less than 25 kg without prior authorization (rotary-wing drones with no weight limit only in rural areas, outside CTRs and restricted airspace)
importantNotes: 📜 NEW FRAMEWORK: ANAC Resolution 550/2025 (effective as of August 2025, amended by Res. 312/2026) replaces Resolution 880/2019. It establishes three categories: Open, Specific and Certified. RAAC Part 100/101/102.

Drones weighing 250 g or more must be registered with ANAC in the Casillero Aeronáutico Digital (CAD) before their first flight — registration is free, online and requires a DNI or passport. Drones weighing less than 250 g (e.g. DJI Mini or Flip) are exempt from registration and licensing (Resolution 550/2025).

Tourists: a valid registration certificate for that drone issued by the civil aviation authority of another ICAO State is accepted (RAAC 100.05); an operator-only registration may not be enough. If your drone is not registered, complete the free digital sworn statement (Declaración Jurada) with ANAC using your passport.

🌳 NATIONAL PARKS AND PROTECTED AREAS: the APN prohibits recreational and sporting use of drones in all its protected areas (APN Res. 9/2021), such as Iguazú, Nahuel Huapi, Los Glaciares or Tierra del Fuego. Professional or scientific use requires prior authorization from the APN.

🏛️ RESTRICTED AREAS: flying is prohibited over the Casa Rosada, the Quinta de Olivos, public buildings and embassies, within 1 nautical mile of military facilities and within the control zones of airports such as Aeroparque and Ezeiza — check the AIP.

💰 PENALTIES: violations are penalized under the Reglamento General de Infracciones de la Aviación Civil, without prejudice to civil or criminal liability. Insurance is mandatory in the Specific and Certified Categories (voluntary in the Open Category).
